mcqs.question: The number of unpaired electrons in an oxygen atom is:
The number of radial nodes in a 2s orbital is:

examShortTricks: Trick 1: Shapes in one phrase each — s: spherical; p: dumb-bell along x, y, z (three px, py, pz).
Trick 2: Orbital vs shell: an orbital holds maximum 2 electrons with opposite spins; 1 s-orbital per shell, 3 p-orbitals from n = 2.
Trick 3: Node question: s-orbital of nth shell has (n−1) nodes — 2s has 1 radial node, 3s has 2.
keyPoints: An orbital is a region of space where the probability of finding the electron is maximum (~90%).
s-orbital: spherical, non-directional; size grows with n (1s < 2s < 3s).
p-orbitals: dumb-bell shaped, three orientations (px, py, pz), first appear at n = 2.
practiceQuestions: Q. Draw the shape of 1s and 2px orbitals and label them. (2 marks) — sphere; dumb-bell along the x-axis with a node at the nucleus.
Q. How many electrons can the p-subshell of L shell hold? (1 mark) — 6 (3 orbitals × 2 electrons).
